chunk_findings.detail: The updated onboarding step points `MIGRATED_WIRE_SHAPES` to `tests/test_api_layer_*.py`, but the split moved the table itself to `tests/api_layer_support.py` (as stated by the updated comments in `ddflow/surfaces/commands/decisions.py` and `ddflow/surfaces/registry/_command.py`). A contributor following this handoff will edit a module matching the glob, such as `tests/test_api_layer_wire.py`, rather than the shared table; the wire-shape test will not see a newly defined table there, so the new tool can remain unpinned or the added row will be ignored.

chunk_findings.detail: The test validates the verification scoring rule by requiring the literal substring `'"verified": bool(results) and not reason and all(r.ok for r in results)'` in the source file of `G._query`. This makes the test depend on textual source form rather than behavior: a semantically equivalent edit to `ddflow/api/gates.py`—for example wrapping the dictionary value in parentheses, splitting the long expression across multiple lines, or changing the comprehension variable name—makes the test fail even though the verification rule is unchanged. Conversely, the exact substring could remain in a comment or docstring while the actual expression is changed, allowing the test to pass even though the real rule no longer implements `bool(results) and not reason and all(r.ok for r in results)`.

chunk_findings.detail:
The loop that is supposed to prove “only REVIEWED may produce `passed`” only inspects the first physical line of each mapping arm:

```python
arm = table[table.index(f"RV.{status}:") : table.index("\n", table.index(f"RV.{status}:"))]
```

If the source formats a mapping across multiple lines, the `"passed"` value is outside `arm` and the assertion passes even though the status maps to a pass. For example, this valid source would satisfy the test while violating its stated invariant:

```python
outcome = {
    RV.UNAVAILABLE: (
        "passed",
    ),
}[best.status]
```

So the test can hide the exact regression it was written to prevent.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_api_layer_reviewers.py:test_no_reviewer_status_maps_to_a_PASS_except_a_real_review

chunk_findings.detail: `test_a_migrated_tool_gives_both_surfaces_the_SAME_data` constructs an in-process `Server(repo)` and calls `handle(...)` for `ddflow_loops` without importing `ddflow.surfaces.cli`. The other test in the same file explicitly says an in-process server needs that import to register the command table. If this test is run in isolation, or before any other test/helper has imported `ddflow.surfaces.cli`, the MCP server may not have the `ddflow_loops` command registered; `handle` then returns a JSON-RPC error result and `reply["result"]` raises `KeyError`, or the extracted text is not the expected JSON. The test can pass only by relying on test-order side effects from the parametrized test that imports `ddflow.surfaces.cli`.

That is exactly the implementation-detail parity check the test says it exists to replace. Given an `api.brief` regression where crash recovery is silently no longer surfaced while the signature default remains `True`, this test still passes and the documented behavior (“crashed work no longer surfaced”) ships undetected.

chunk_findings.detail: `test_recording_out_of_order_under_warn_records_the_violation` inspects only `next((repo / ".ddflow" / "events").glob("*.jsonl"))`, i.e. one arbitrary JSONL shard. When `.ddflow/events/` contains more than one shard — which the variable name “shard” and the glob itself acknowledge is possible — the `gate.out_of_order` event may be written to a different shard than the one chosen by `next`, whose iteration order is not deterministic. In that case line 73 fails with “the violation was not recorded”, even though `api.gate_record` correctly recorded it.

chunk_findings.detail: The assertion `assert reply["result"]["isError"] is False, reply` is overconstrained for the behavior under test. `CallToolResult.isError` is optional and may legitimately be omitted on a successful non-error result; the same file’s `test_a_refusal_is_not_an_error_on_the_typed_path` explicitly accepts `False` or `None` for non-error outcomes. With a correct successful `ddflow_update` clear where the MCP result omits the optional `isError` key, this line raises `KeyError: 'isError'` (or fails if the value is `None`), spuriously failing the test even though the clear succeeded.

chunk_findings.detail: The HANDOFF instruction now tells the reader to add a row to `MIGRATED_WIRE_SHAPES` in `tests/test_api_layer_*.py`, but the other changed references in this diff state that the `MIGRATED_WIRE_SHAPES` table lives in `tests/api_layer_support.py` (`ddflow/surfaces/commands/decisions.py` and `ddflow/surfaces/registry/_command.py`). A developer following the HANDOFF will edit a `tests/test_api_layer_*.py` module instead of the shared table, so the wire-shape row will not be picked up by `test_every_typed_tool_has_a_wire_shape_row` and the parity/wire-shape check can still fail.

chunk_findings.detail: The test claims to pin the exit-code table so that “only a real review with no findings is success,” but the `exits` assertions check only `RV.UNAVAILABLE`, `RV.ERROR`, and `RV.PARTIAL`; they never check the `RV.REVIEWED` arm. If the `exit_code` mapping in `A._review_gate` is changed so that `RV.REVIEWED` is omitted, or so that it maps unconditionally to `O.NOTHING`, this test still passes because the other three arms remain present and the outcome-table assertion still holds. For example, deleting the `RV.REVIEWED` line from the `exit_code` dict would make completed reviews raise `KeyError` at runtime (or, if changed to `O.NOTHING`, make a review with findings exit as success), while this test remains green.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_api_layer_reviewers.py:test_no_reviewer_status_maps_to_a_PASS_except_a_real_review

chunk_findings.detail: This test calls the in-process MCP `Server` without importing `ddflow.surfaces.cli`, even though the first test in the same file explicitly says an in-process server needs that import (Bc782b6c724). If this test is run in isolation, e.g. `pytest tests/test_api_layer_wire.py::test_a_migrated_tool_gives_both_surfaces_the_SAME_data`, or in an order where no earlier test has already imported `ddflow.surfaces.cli`, the command table may not be registered and the MCP reply will not be the CLI-equivalent JSON. The test then does `start = min(..., default=-1)` and immediately `_json.loads(text[start:])` without checking `start != -1`, so a non-JSON error response produces a confusing `JSONDecodeError` instead of a clear contract failure, and a JSON error body makes the exact comparison fail. Thus the test is order-dependent and can fail or fail opaquely when run without the side effect of another test.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_api_layer_wire.py::test_a_migrated_tool_gives_both_surfaces_the_SAME_data

chunk_findings.detail: The test claims to guard the bug where the MCP/JSON surface failed to receive the `ungoverned` warning, but it only exercises the application-layer call `api.decision_add` and inspects `Outcome.data`. It never invokes `run_cli` or `ddflow.surfaces.mcp.Server`. Therefore a regression in the CLI or MCP projection that drops the `ungoverned` field while `api.decision_add` still computes it would leave this test green, exactly the surface bug the docstring says it prevents.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_api_layer_writes.py:test_a_decision_with_no_globs_warns_on_BOTH_surfaces

chunk_findings.detail: The assertion was repointed from `tests/test_api_layer.py` to `tests/api_layer_support.py`, but `api_layer_support.py` is a helper module rather than a test suite. The surrounding code treats `out.data["tests"]` as a list of test suites (it checks for `tests/test_implement_command.py` and calls `.index()` on the list), so after the split this test will call `suites.index("tests/api_layer_support.py")` on a list that does not contain that non-test helper and raise `ValueError`. Even if the command’s list does include non-test Python files, the check no longer pins ordering against an API-layer test suite and therefore no longer preserves the original guarantee.

chunk_findings.detail: `test_recording_out_of_order_under_warn_records_the_violation` reads only the first shard returned by `next((repo / ".ddflow" / "events").glob("*.jsonl"))`. The event store may contain multiple JSONL shards (the glob pattern and the variable name `shard` indicate that), so the `gate.out_of_order` event can be written to a shard other than the one selected. Given, for example, separate `task.jsonl` and `gate.jsonl` shards, `next` may return the task shard, the recorded gate event is in the other shard, and the assertion fails even though the behavior under test was correct.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_api_layer_pipeline.py:69

chunk_findings.detail: This test parses the exact source text of `ddflow/api/review.py` by searching for literal substrings such as `outcome = {`, `}[best.status]`, `exit_code = {`, and `RV.REVIEWED: ("failed" if best.findings else "passed")`. A harmless formatting/refactor input—e.g. Black wrapping the dictionary subscript across lines or using single quotes—will cause `src.index(...)` to raise `ValueError` and fail the suite even though the production behavior is unchanged. This makes the new test depend on source layout instead of actual behavior, so the split is not purely a test-file split and will break under a normal formatter.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_api_layer_reviewers.py:test_no_reviewer_status_maps_to_a_PASS_except_a_real_review

chunk_findings.detail: The test is explicitly named and grouped as exercising the MCP surface (the neighboring `test_recording_a_decision_over_mcp_records_it` does call `Server(repo).handle`), but this test only calls `api.decision_supersede` directly. A regression in the MCP `tools/call` handler for `ddflow_decision_supersede` that mapped the API’s `FAIL` exit to `isError=False`—or mishandled the `by` argument—would leave this test green. That silently changes/drops the MCP-surface assertion, violating the stated “no test dropped or changed” intent.

On that line `list.index` raises `ValueError: 'tests/api_layer_support.py' is not in list`, failing `test_prose_pins`. The reference should use one of the new `tests/test_api_layer_*.py` topic modules that is actually included in `suites`.

chunk_findings.detail: In `tests/api_layer_support.py`, `TEXT_BODIED` includes `"ddflow_brief"`, but `"ddflow_brief"` is also mapped in `MIGRATED_WIRE_SHAPES` on line 118 (`"ddflow_brief": (["brief"], {}),`). When tests iterate over `MIGRATED_WIRE_SHAPES` to test tools and check them against `TEXT_BODIED`, this redundancy/overlap causes `ddflow_brief` to be treated as both a standard JSON-bodied wire-shape comparison and a text-bodied comparison simultaneously, leading to test assertion failures or incorrect type parsing during wire-shape verification.

chunk_findings.detail: The test file `tests/test_api_layer.py` has been completely deleted in this diff (lines 1 to 1828 removed), but the project guidance `[r-ddflow-self-assessment]` requires filing findings for bugs of ddflow itself, misbehavior, or missing features discovered during agent runs, and the intent states this is a "Pure test-file split... no test dropped or changed". However, deleting `tests/test_api_layer.py` entirely while moving its contents to 7 new files means any external script or CI check referencing `tests/test_api_layer.py` directly will fail with a file-not-found error unless updated.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_api_layer.py

chunk_findings.detail: In `test_a_bug_cannot_be_closed_without_a_regression_test`, `(repo / "tests").mkdir(exist_ok=True)` creates a `tests` directory directly inside the test fixture `repo` (which is a temporary repository directory), and writes `tests/test_events.py` there. However, pytest runs tests from the project root directory, not from inside the temporary `repo` directory, so when `api.bug_fixed` verifies the existence of the regression test file (`tests/test_events.py`), it checks the main project's `tests` directory instead of the `repo` path, or vice versa depending on working directory. If `api.bug_fixed` checks relative to the repo root, `tests/test_events.py` placed inside `repo` will not be found if it checks the process working directory, or if it resolves relative to `repo`, writing to `repo / "tests"` may fail or succeed incorrectly depending on the implementation. Given input `repo`, `api.bug_fixed(repo, bug, regression_test="tests/test_events.py::test_seq")` can fail with a file-not-found error if `api` checks `Path(regression_test)` relative to the current working directory.

chunk_findings.detail: `test_no_reviewer_status_maps_to_a_PASS_except_a_real_review` inspects source code of `ddflow.api.review` (`inspect.getsource(A._review_gate)`) to find a variable name `outcome = {` and asserts on its contents. In Python, local variable names inside functions are implementation details that can be renamed, refactored, or compiled without preserving exact source text matching `outcome = {`, making this test brittle and prone to breaking during internal refactoring without actual regression in behavior.

`test_a_migrated_tool_reproduces_its_CLI_json_exactly` modifies `probe` after running the CLI command via `probe.write_text("#!/bin/sh
exit 0
", "utf-8")`, but it does not update the companions cache (`companions._write_cache`) to reflect the new probe status before invoking the MCP server. Consequently, when the MCP server runs, the companion detection still uses the old cached result from when the file was unexecutable (`not a program
`), causing the MCP and CLI surfaces to receive different companion states and making the parity check flaky or dependent on the caching implementation.

chunk_findings.detail: In `tests/test_prose_pins.py`, the test checks `suites.index("tests/test_implement_command.py") < suites.index("tests/api_layer_support.py")`. However, `tests/api_layer_support.py` is a support module (not a test file itself, starting with `test_`), but `tests/test_api_layer.py` was split into multiple test files such as `tests/test_api_layer_correctness.py`, `tests/test_api_layer_knowledge.py`, etc., none of which are checked here. If `tests/api_layer_support.py` happens to sort alphabetically *after* `tests/test_implement_command.py`, this assertion might accidentally pass or fail depending on path ordering, but repointing it to a support module instead of the actual API layer test files defeats the prose pin's check of test suite ordering.

chunk_findings.detail: The updated onboarding step points `MIGRATED_WIRE_SHAPES` to `tests/test_api_layer_*.py`, but the split moved the table itself to `tests/api_layer_support.py` (as stated by the updated comments in `ddflow/surfaces/commands/decisions.py` and `ddflow/surfaces/registry/_command.py`). A contributor following this handoff will edit a module matching the glob, such as `tests/test_api_layer_wire.py`, rather than the shared table; the wire-shape test will not see a newly defined table there, so the new tool can remain unpinned or the added row will be ignored.
chunk_findings.title: docs/HANDOFF.md:379

chunk_findings.detail: The test validates the verification scoring rule by requiring the literal substring `'"verified": bool(results) and not reason and all(r.ok for r in results)'` in the source file of `G._query`. This makes the test depend on textual source form rather than behavior: a semantically equivalent edit to `ddflow/api/gates.py`—for example wrapping the dictionary value in parentheses, splitting the long expression across multiple lines, or changing the comprehension variable name—makes the test fail even though the verification rule is unchanged. Conversely, the exact substring could remain in a comment or docstring while the actual expression is changed, allowing the test to pass even though the real rule no longer implements `bool(results) and not reason and all(r.ok for r in results)`.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_api_layer_pipeline.py:test_verification_with_no_results_is_never_a_pass

chunk_findings.detail:
The loop that is supposed to prove “only REVIEWED may produce `passed`” only inspects the first physical line of each mapping arm:

```python
arm = table[table.index(f"RV.{status}:") : table.index("\n", table.index(f"RV.{status}:"))]
```

If the source formats a mapping across multiple lines, the `"passed"` value is outside `arm` and the assertion passes even though the status maps to a pass. For example, this valid source would satisfy the test while violating its stated invariant:

```python
outcome = {
    RV.UNAVAILABLE: (
        "passed",
    ),
}[best.status]
```

So the test can hide the exact regression it was written to prevent.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_api_layer_reviewers.py:test_no_reviewer_status_maps_to_a_PASS_except_a_real_review

chunk_findings.detail: `test_a_migrated_tool_gives_both_surfaces_the_SAME_data` constructs an in-process `Server(repo)` and calls `handle(...)` for `ddflow_loops` without importing `ddflow.surfaces.cli`. The other test in the same file explicitly says an in-process server needs that import to register the command table. If this test is run in isolation, or before any other test/helper has imported `ddflow.surfaces.cli`, the MCP server may not have the `ddflow_loops` command registered; `handle` then returns a JSON-RPC error result and `reply["result"]` raises `KeyError`, or the extracted text is not the expected JSON. The test can pass only by relying on test-order side effects from the parametrized test that imports `ddflow.surfaces.cli`.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_api_layer_wire.py:191

chunk_findings.detail: The assertion was repointed from `tests/test_api_layer.py`, an actual test suite, to `tests/api_layer_support.py`, a helper module with no tests. `out.data["tests"]` is the list of test suites; after the split the API-layer suites are the new `tests/test_api_layer_*.py` modules, not the support file. If the command returns only test suites, `suites.index("tests/api_layer_support.py")` raises `ValueError: 'tests/api_layer_support.py' is not in list`. Even if a prose scanner includes non-test paths, the test no longer pins the intended ordering of the API-layer test suites, so the original guarantee can regress while this test passes.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_prose_pins.py:221

chunk_findings.detail: The updated instruction says to add a row to `MIGRATED_WIRE_SHAPES` in `tests/test_api_layer_*.py`, but the table actually lives in `tests/api_layer_support.py` per this same change (`ddflow/surfaces/commands/decisions.py` now points to `tests/api_layer_support.py::MIGRATED_WIRE_SHAPES`, and `ddflow/surfaces/registry/_command.py` says the table is in `tests/api_layer_support.py`). A contributor following this instruction will look in the wrong file, because the glob `test_api_layer_*.py` does not match `api_layer_support.py`.
chunk_findings.title: docs/HANDOFF.md:379

chunk_findings.detail: The test claims to enforce each default by what it does, but for `DEFAULT_CHECK_RECOVERY` it only asserts `inspect.signature(api.brief).parameters["check_recovery"].default is True`. That is exactly the implementation-detail parity check the test says it exists to replace. Given an `api.brief` regression where crash recovery is silently no longer surfaced while the signature default remains `True`, this test still passes and the documented behavior (“crashed work no longer surfaced”) ships undetected.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_api_layer_knowledge.py:test_each_default_VALUE_is_the_one_the_behaviour_needs

chunk_findings.detail: `test_recording_out_of_order_under_warn_records_the_violation` inspects only `next((repo / ".ddflow" / "events").glob("*.jsonl"))`, i.e. one arbitrary JSONL shard. When `.ddflow/events/` contains more than one shard — which the variable name “shard” and the glob itself acknowledge is possible — the `gate.out_of_order` event may be written to a different shard than the one chosen by `next`, whose iteration order is not deterministic. In that case line 73 fails with “the violation was not recorded”, even though `api.gate_record` correctly recorded it.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_api_layer_pipeline.py:71

chunk_findings.detail: The assertion `assert reply["result"]["isError"] is False, reply` is overconstrained for the behavior under test. `CallToolResult.isError` is optional and may legitimately be omitted on a successful non-error result; the same file’s `test_a_refusal_is_not_an_error_on_the_typed_path` explicitly accepts `False` or `None` for non-error outcomes. With a correct successful `ddflow_update` clear where the MCP result omits the optional `isError` key, this line raises `KeyError: 'isError'` (or fails if the value is `None`), spuriously failing the test even though the clear succeeded.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_api_layer_typed.py:test_clearing_a_field_over_mcp_works_on_whichever_path_is_live

chunk_findings.detail: `sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1])))` has an extra closing parenthesis. Parsing the file raises `SyntaxError: unmatched ')'`, so pytest cannot collect or run any tests in this module. The line should end with `parents[1]))`, not `parents[1])))`.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_api_layer_wire.py:10

chunk_findings.detail: The test’s name and docstring claim the ungoverned warning is emitted on both the CLI and MCP surfaces, and that “both surfaces read it,” but the test only calls `api.decision_add` and asserts fields on the returned Outcome (`without.data["ungoverned"]` and `with_globs.data["ungoverned"]`). It never invokes the CLI or the MCP `Server.handle` surface. A change that silently drops the warning emission from both renderers while leaving the Outcome field intact would keep this test green, so it does not actually verify the behavior it claims to test.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_api_layer_writes.py::test_a_decision_with_no_globs_warns_on_BOTH_surfaces

chunk_findings.detail: The assertion now looks for `"tests/api_layer_support.py"` in `suites`, but that new file is a support/helper module and does not match the default pytest test-file pattern (`test_*.py`/`*_test.py`), unlike the old `tests/test_api_layer.py`. If `out.data["tests"]` is a collected test-suite list, `api_layer_support.py` will not be present, so `suites.index("tests/api_layer_support.py")` raises `ValueError: 'tests/api_layer_support.py' is not in list` and the test fails when run after the split.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_prose_pins.py:221

chunk_findings.detail: `ddflow_session_asks` is listed in `WRITES_NOT_COMPARABLE`, but its docstring and project architecture describe it as a read operation ("the read `asks`"), which contradicts the set's invariant that all listed tools write state and therefore cannot be invoked twice safely.
chunk_findings.title: tests/api_layer_support.py:270

chunk_findings.detail: `test_prose_pins.py` checks that `tests/test_implement_command.py` comes before `tests/test_api_layer.py` in test suites. The change replaces `tests/test_api_layer.py` with `tests/api_layer_support.py` in the assertion, but `tests/api_layer_support.py` is not a test file (it starts with `api_layer_support.py`, not `test_`), so when pytest runs or discovers test suites, `tests/api_layer_support.py` will not be in `suites`, causing `suites.index("tests/api_layer_support.py")` to raise a `ValueError` during test execution.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_prose_pins.py:221

chunk_findings.detail: The HANDOFF instruction now tells the reader to add a row to `MIGRATED_WIRE_SHAPES` in `tests/test_api_layer_*.py`, but the other changed references in this diff state that the `MIGRATED_WIRE_SHAPES` table lives in `tests/api_layer_support.py` (`ddflow/surfaces/commands/decisions.py` and `ddflow/surfaces/registry/_command.py`). A developer following the HANDOFF will edit a `tests/test_api_layer_*.py` module instead of the shared table, so the wire-shape row will not be picked up by `test_every_typed_tool_has_a_wire_shape_row` and the parity/wire-shape check can still fail.
chunk_findings.title: docs/HANDOFF.md:379

chunk_findings.detail: The test claims to pin the exit-code table so that “only a real review with no findings is success,” but the `exits` assertions check only `RV.UNAVAILABLE`, `RV.ERROR`, and `RV.PARTIAL`; they never check the `RV.REVIEWED` arm. If the `exit_code` mapping in `A._review_gate` is changed so that `RV.REVIEWED` is omitted, or so that it maps unconditionally to `O.NOTHING`, this test still passes because the other three arms remain present and the outcome-table assertion still holds. For example, deleting the `RV.REVIEWED` line from the `exit_code` dict would make completed reviews raise `KeyError` at runtime (or, if changed to `O.NOTHING`, make a review with findings exit as success), while this test remains green.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_api_layer_reviewers.py:test_no_reviewer_status_maps_to_a_PASS_except_a_real_review

chunk_findings.detail: This test calls the in-process MCP `Server` without importing `ddflow.surfaces.cli`, even though the first test in the same file explicitly says an in-process server needs that import (Bc782b6c724). If this test is run in isolation, e.g. `pytest tests/test_api_layer_wire.py::test_a_migrated_tool_gives_both_surfaces_the_SAME_data`, or in an order where no earlier test has already imported `ddflow.surfaces.cli`, the command table may not be registered and the MCP reply will not be the CLI-equivalent JSON. The test then does `start = min(..., default=-1)` and immediately `_json.loads(text[start:])` without checking `start != -1`, so a non-JSON error response produces a confusing `JSONDecodeError` instead of a clear contract failure, and a JSON error body makes the exact comparison fail. Thus the test is order-dependent and can fail or fail opaquely when run without the side effect of another test.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_api_layer_wire.py::test_a_migrated_tool_gives_both_surfaces_the_SAME_data

chunk_findings.detail: The test claims to guard the bug where the MCP/JSON surface failed to receive the `ungoverned` warning, but it only exercises the application-layer call `api.decision_add` and inspects `Outcome.data`. It never invokes `run_cli` or `ddflow.surfaces.mcp.Server`. Therefore a regression in the CLI or MCP projection that drops the `ungoverned` field while `api.decision_add` still computes it would leave this test green, exactly the surface bug the docstring says it prevents.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_api_layer_writes.py:test_a_decision_with_no_globs_warns_on_BOTH_surfaces

chunk_findings.detail: The assertion was repointed from `tests/test_api_layer.py` to `tests/api_layer_support.py`, but `api_layer_support.py` is a helper module rather than a test suite. The surrounding code treats `out.data["tests"]` as a list of test suites (it checks for `tests/test_implement_command.py` and calls `.index()` on the list), so after the split this test will call `suites.index("tests/api_layer_support.py")` on a list that does not contain that non-test helper and raise `ValueError`. Even if the command’s list does include non-test Python files, the check no longer pins ordering against an API-layer test suite and therefore no longer preserves the original guarantee.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_prose_pins.py:221

chunk_findings.detail: The handoff now tells readers to add a row to `MIGRATED_WIRE_SHAPES` in `tests/test_api_layer_*.py`, but that glob does not match the support file where the table actually lives. The updated comment in `ddflow/surfaces/registry/_command.py` in this same change says the table is in `tests/api_layer_support.py`, so a developer following `docs/HANDOFF.md` will look in the wrong file and not find `MIGRATED_WIRE_SHAPES`.
chunk_findings.title: docs/HANDOFF.md:379

chunk_findings.detail: `test_recording_out_of_order_under_warn_records_the_violation` reads only the first shard returned by `next((repo / ".ddflow" / "events").glob("*.jsonl"))`. The event store may contain multiple JSONL shards (the glob pattern and the variable name `shard` indicate that), so the `gate.out_of_order` event can be written to a shard other than the one selected. Given, for example, separate `task.jsonl` and `gate.jsonl` shards, `next` may return the task shard, the recorded gate event is in the other shard, and the assertion fails even though the behavior under test was correct.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_api_layer_pipeline.py:69

chunk_findings.detail: This test parses the exact source text of `ddflow/api/review.py` by searching for literal substrings such as `outcome = {`, `}[best.status]`, `exit_code = {`, and `RV.REVIEWED: ("failed" if best.findings else "passed")`. A harmless formatting/refactor input—e.g. Black wrapping the dictionary subscript across lines or using single quotes—will cause `src.index(...)` to raise `ValueError` and fail the suite even though the production behavior is unchanged. This makes the new test depend on source layout instead of actual behavior, so the split is not purely a test-file split and will break under a normal formatter.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_api_layer_reviewers.py:test_no_reviewer_status_maps_to_a_PASS_except_a_real_review

chunk_findings.detail: The test is explicitly named and grouped as exercising the MCP surface (the neighboring `test_recording_a_decision_over_mcp_records_it` does call `Server(repo).handle`), but this test only calls `api.decision_supersede` directly. A regression in the MCP `tools/call` handler for `ddflow_decision_supersede` that mapped the API’s `FAIL` exit to `isError=False`—or mishandled the `by` argument—would leave this test green. That silently changes/drops the MCP-surface assertion, violating the stated “no test dropped or changed” intent.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_api_layer_writes.py:test_superseding_over_mcp_refuses_without_a_replacement

chunk_findings.detail: The repointed assertion calls `suites.index("tests/api_layer_support.py")`. `api_layer_support.py` is a support/helper module, not a test suite, and does not match pytest's `test_*.py` discovery pattern, so it will not be present in `out.data["tests"]`. On that line `list.index` raises `ValueError: 'tests/api_layer_support.py' is not in list`, failing `test_prose_pins`. The reference should use one of the new `tests/test_api_layer_*.py` topic modules that is actually included in `suites`.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_prose_pins.py:222

chunk_findings.detail: In `tests/api_layer_support.py`, `TEXT_BODIED` includes `"ddflow_brief"`, but `"ddflow_brief"` is also mapped in `MIGRATED_WIRE_SHAPES` on line 118 (`"ddflow_brief": (["brief"], {}),`). When tests iterate over `MIGRATED_WIRE_SHAPES` to test tools and check them against `TEXT_BODIED`, this redundancy/overlap causes `ddflow_brief` to be treated as both a standard JSON-bodied wire-shape comparison and a text-bodied comparison simultaneously, leading to test assertion failures or incorrect type parsing during wire-shape verification.
chunk_findings.title: tests/api_layer_support.py:155

chunk_findings.detail: The test file `tests/test_api_layer.py` has been completely deleted in this diff (lines 1 to 1828 removed), but the project guidance `[r-ddflow-self-assessment]` requires filing findings for bugs of ddflow itself, misbehavior, or missing features discovered during agent runs, and the intent states this is a "Pure test-file split... no test dropped or changed". However, deleting `tests/test_api_layer.py` entirely while moving its contents to 7 new files means any external script or CI check referencing `tests/test_api_layer.py` directly will fail with a file-not-found error unless updated.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_api_layer.py

chunk_findings.detail: In `test_a_bug_cannot_be_closed_without_a_regression_test`, `(repo / "tests").mkdir(exist_ok=True)` creates a `tests` directory directly inside the test fixture `repo` (which is a temporary repository directory), and writes `tests/test_events.py` there. However, pytest runs tests from the project root directory, not from inside the temporary `repo` directory, so when `api.bug_fixed` verifies the existence of the regression test file (`tests/test_events.py`), it checks the main project's `tests` directory instead of the `repo` path, or vice versa depending on working directory. If `api.bug_fixed` checks relative to the repo root, `tests/test_events.py` placed inside `repo` will not be found if it checks the process working directory, or if it resolves relative to `repo`, writing to `repo / "tests"` may fail or succeed incorrectly depending on the implementation. Given input `repo`, `api.bug_fixed(repo, bug, regression_test="tests/test_events.py::test_seq")` can fail with a file-not-found error if `api` checks `Path(regression_test)` relative to the current working directory.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_api_layer_knowledge.py:180

chunk_findings.detail: `test_no_reviewer_status_maps_to_a_PASS_except_a_real_review` inspects source code of `ddflow.api.review` (`inspect.getsource(A._review_gate)`) to find a variable name `outcome = {` and asserts on its contents. In Python, local variable names inside functions are implementation details that can be renamed, refactored, or compiled without preserving exact source text matching `outcome = {`, making this test brittle and prone to breaking during internal refactoring without actual regression in behavior.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_api_layer_reviewers.py:126

chunk_findings.detail: `test_clearing_a_field_over_mcp_works_on_whichever_path_is_live` sends `{"name": "ddflow_update", "arguments": {"id": "B", "needs": ""}}` over MCP, but `api.update` expects `needs=[]` (a list) or equivalent to clear a field; passing a string `""` over MCP fails input validation or does not clear the field as intended by the test's own docstring explanation of the `clearable` fix, leading to a test failure or false pass depending on argument coercion.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_api_layer_typed.py:100

chunk_findings.detail:
`test_a_migrated_tool_reproduces_its_CLI_json_exactly` modifies `probe` after running the CLI command via `probe.write_text("#!/bin/sh
exit 0
", "utf-8")`, but it does not update the companions cache (`companions._write_cache`) to reflect the new probe status before invoking the MCP server. Consequently, when the MCP server runs, the companion detection still uses the old cached result from when the file was unexecutable (`not a program
`), causing the MCP and CLI surfaces to receive different companion states and making the parity check flaky or dependent on the caching implementation.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_api_layer_wire.py:108

chunk_findings.detail: In `tests/test_prose_pins.py`, the test checks `suites.index("tests/test_implement_command.py") < suites.index("tests/api_layer_support.py")`. However, `tests/api_layer_support.py` is a support module (not a test file itself, starting with `test_`), but `tests/test_api_layer.py` was split into multiple test files such as `tests/test_api_layer_correctness.py`, `tests/test_api_layer_knowledge.py`, etc., none of which are checked here. If `tests/api_layer_support.py` happens to sort alphabetically *after* `tests/test_implement_command.py`, this assertion might accidentally pass or fail depending on path ordering, but repointing it to a support module instead of the actual API layer test files defeats the prose pin's check of test suite ordering.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_prose_pins.py:221
